title: Proposed Rule to Require Commercial Vehicles and Buses to Have Rear View Cameras Installed
what_it_is: Proposed Rule to Require Commercial Vehicles and Buses to Have Rear View Cameras Installed

sections.label: Blind spot device requirement
sections.summary: LTA requires heavy goods vehicles and buses to install blind-spot mirrors and camera monitor systems covering blind spots and rear view.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: LTA requires all heavy goods vehicles and buses to install devices that cover the vehicle's blind spot areas, as well as the rear view.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: These devices include blind-spot mirrors and camera monitor systems, which include rear-view cameras, and the objective is to ensure that the driver has sufficient field of vision and awareness of persons near their vehicle.

sections.label: Rules and penalties
sections.summary: The requirement falls under the Road Traffic (Motor Vehicles, Construction and Use) Rules, with fines and jail for non-compliance at annual inspection.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Yes, this requirement for heavy goods vehicles and buses to be equipped with such devices to cover blind spots, as well as the rear view, is under the Road Traffic (Motor Vehicles, Construction and Use) Rules.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: During their annual inspection, if they are found not to have complied, there could be a penalty imposed, a fine as well as jail term.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The first offence is up to a $1,000 fine and three months' jail; and it is double for repeat offences.

sections.label: Japan and EU requirements
sections.summary: Japan and the EU implemented requirements for devices to check vehicle rears, and Singapore is monitoring and reviewing these developments.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: In addition to that, in Japan and Europe last year – in June 2022, Japan has required its automakers to equip all their vehicles, including new goods vehicles, with devices to enable the drivers to check on the rear of the vehicle.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: It could be other devices – sensors, for instance, or even mirrors, perhaps of a different type.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: And it is only implemented for new models immediately from June; and for existing models, from May 2024.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: In July, EU also announced and implemented a similar set of requirements, but it is not for existing registered vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: So, we are also closely monitoring these developments and looking at reviewing this and studying whether it is feasible to add on additional safety requirements.
